test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A car covers 60 km at a speed of 84 km/h. If the average speed for the whole journey is 72 km/h, then the speed of the car for the next 60 km of the journey is:
solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered in the first part = 60 km at a speed of 84 km/h.

Distance covered in the second part = 60 km.

Average speed for the whole journey = 72 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken to cover the first 60 km = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time taken for the first 60 km = 60 / 84 hours

Total distance for the whole journey = 60 + 60 = 120 km

Given average speed for the whole journey = 72 km/h

Total time for the whole journey = Total distance / Average speed

⇒ Total time for 120 km = 120 / 72 hours

Let the speed for the next 60 km be x km/h.

Time taken for the next 60 km = 60 / x hours

According to the given information:

Total time = Time for first 60 km + Time for next 60 km

⇒ 120 / 72 = (60 / 84) + (60 / x)

Solving for x:

⇒ 5 / 3 = (5 / 7) + (60 / x)

⇒ 60 / x = (5 / 3) - (5 / 7)

⇒ 60 / x = (35 - 15) / 21

⇒ 60 / x = 20 / 21

⇒ x = (60 × 21) / 20

⇒ x = 63 km/h

**The speed of the car for the next 60 km of the journey is 63 km/h.**
